title: The derived transpose of a termwise mate and its comparison unit
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal A',\mathcal B'$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] in a common universe [def-weil-size-convention], with derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Write $K^+(\mathcal C)$ for bounded-below cochain complexes modulo chain homotopy, $q:K^+(\mathcal C)\to D^+(\mathcal C)$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms, and $K(F)$ for termwise application of an additive functor. Let $L:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, $L':\mathcal B'\to\mathcal A'$, $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B'$ and $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ be exact additive functors. Put $E=D(L)$, $E'=D(L')$, $T=D(G)$ and $S=D(H)$, with their canonical natural localization isomorphisms $\phi_{F,V}:D(F)(qV)\xrightarrow{\sim}qK(F)V$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Let $\sigma:L'G\to HL$ be an arbitrary natural transformation, and let $\sigma^K:K(L')K(G)\to K(H)K(L)$ be its termwise transformation on $K^+$. Assume $\mathcal A,\mathcal A'$ have enough injectives, meaning that every object embeds into an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Give additive right adjoints $R,R'$ and adjunctions $L\dashv R$, $L'\dashv R'$. Write $\eta'^K,\varepsilon^K$ for their termwise homotopy unit and counit [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Let $U=\mathbf R R$, $U'=\mathbf R R'$ with natural comparison maps $\alpha:qK(R)\to Uq$, $\alpha':qK(R')\to U'q$ [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Use the canonical derived adjunctions $E\dashv U$ and $E'\dashv U'$, with primed unit $\eta'^D$ and unprimed counit $\varepsilon^D$, normalized by the unit and counit identities of [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction]. Let $b:GR\to R'H$ be the ordinary mate of $\sigma$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For each $P\in K^+(\mathcal A)$ put $N=K(R)P$, $M=K(G)N$, $W=K(H)P$, $Z=qM$, and $d=K(H)(\varepsilon^K_P)\circ\sigma^K_N:K(L')M\to W$. Then
$$K(R')(d)\circ\eta'^K_M=K(b)_P,$$
and, in $D^+(\mathcal B')$,
$$U'(q(d))\circ U'(\phi_{L',M})\circ\eta'^D_Z=\alpha'_W\circ q(K(b)_P).$$
The first equality uses the homotopy classes of the genuine termwise chain maps. In particular their degree-$n$ components are $R'(H(\varepsilon_{P^n}))\circ R'(\sigma_{R(P^n)})\circ\eta'_{G(R(P^n))}=b_{P^n}$, where $\varepsilon,\eta'$ are the ordinary counit and primed unit. The second equality holds for arbitrary bounded-below $P$; neither injectivity of $W$ nor invertibility of $\alpha'_W$ is required. No derived square or mate of a derived square is part of this assertion.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], the unit and counit in $K^+$ are represented by their termwise chain maps. In degree $n$, the composite $K(R')(d)\circ\eta'^K_M$ is $R'(H(\varepsilon_{P^n}))\circ R'(\sigma_{R(P^n)})\circ\eta'_{G(R(P^n))}$, using functoriality and the definition of $d$. This is precisely $b_{P^n}$ by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Thus the two genuine chain maps agree in every degree, hence their homotopy classes agree: $K(R')(d)\circ\eta'^K_M=K(b)_P$.

Apply the unit identity of [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction] to $L'\dashv R'$ and $M\in K^+(\mathcal B')$. Its hypotheses hold because $L'$ is exact and $\mathcal A'$ has enough injectives. With $Z=qM$ it gives $U'(\phi_{L',M})\circ\eta'^D_Z=\alpha'_{K(L')M}\circ q(\eta'^K_M)$. Postcompose this equality with $U'(q(d))$.

The comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] is a natural transformation on all of $K^+(\mathcal A')$. Its naturality at $d:K(L')M\to W$ reads $U'(q(d))\circ\alpha'_{K(L')M}=\alpha'_W\circ q(K(R')(d))$. Substitute this into step 2, use that $q$ preserves composition, and substitute step 1. The resulting right side is $\alpha'_W\circ q(K(R')(d)\circ\eta'^K_M)=\alpha'_W\circ q(K(b)_P)$, which is the required second equality. Naturality applies without injectivity of $W$, and no comparison map was inverted.
